::: {.callout-important title="This setup no longer applies"}
This page describes a removed setup: SCGSim `1.1.0rc1` with a fork of Palace.
Today SCGSim 3 runs stock Palace 0.18.1 and needs no fork; to compute modes
with it, follow [Modes with Palace](../../guides/modes-palace.qmd) after
[Install SCGSim](../../start/install.qmd). This page only explains how an
older result was made.
:::

The Circular Pad Uniform-port study ran a Palace Eigenmode calculation on a
circular pad whose boundary was authored as curves. It used SCGSim
`1.1.0rc1`, an OrcaPen SC PDK revision as the producer of the model, and a
Palace fork. Reproduce it only in a project of its own.

## Select the source and PDK revisions

| Role | Revision |
|---|---|
| PDK that produced the executed run | [`c79b91ef882079d937fce20129f3cbd477e8438d`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/c79b91ef882079d937fce20129f3cbd477e8438d) |
| SCGSim of the run (`1.1.0rc1`, with the curved-source APIs that `1.0.2` lacks) | [`2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/tree/2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71) |
| Later PDK revision with the teaching notebook and the evidence | [`ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52) |

The teaching notebook, [`palace_eigenmode.qmd`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.qmd)
and its [derived notebook](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.ipynb),
belongs to the later revision and did not produce the run; its
[evidence README](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/evidence/README.md)
names the producer. Create a separate project with the producer and the
runtime of the run:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 curved-source-study
cd curved-source-study
uv add 'scgsim[palace,visualization] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@c79b91ef882079d937fce20129f3cbd477e8438d' \
  ipykernel
```

Check: `uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('scgsim'))"` prints `1.1.0rc1`.

## Native Palace for this curved Uniform port {#native-palace-for-this-curved-uniform-port}

The study used the Palace fork at revision
[`4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37`](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/tree/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37),
or a later one with its
[curved-port extent correction](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/blob/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37/palace/utils/geodata_impl.cpp).
The Python package does not install Palace; configure that build's MPI
wrapper as the executable.

The published run record reports mode 1 at `5.573354161115 GHz` after four
refinements and five solve and estimate snapshots. Its final native indicator
is `0.1186681863426` against a configured `0.02`, and its native log records
PCG warnings.
